message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 (total ~$9,812).

**What I did and why:** I researched Apple's just-reported fiscal 2024 results from two primary sources — Apple's Q4 FY2024 press release (quarter ended September 28, 2024) and the FY2024 Form 10-K filed with the SEC — and they were consistent: fourth-quarter revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year revenue of $391,035 million (vs. $383,285 million in FY2023), with **net income for fiscal 2024 of $93,736 million (~$93.7 billion)**, or $6.08 per diluted share, alongside operating income of $123,216 million. Net income was down modestly from FY2023's $96,995 million, but that decline was driven by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge rather than operating deterioration — revenue still grew and operating profit remained very strong — so I viewed the print as solid and saw no reason to stay out, deciding to buy. AAPL's quote at the time was $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so I placed a single limit buy that stays inside your mandate on every dimension: an AAPL buy (permitted ticker, buy-only), 44 shares at a $223.00 limit — only ~0.13% above the last price, i.e. close to market — for a total of roughly $9,812, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, funded entirely from the account's existing $50,000 cash with no money moved out. I made no MSFT trade and placed no other orders today.
